* -110 dBm means a threshold lower than -110 dBm

Short description:
Indicates the status of the neighbor relation.

unavailable:
Indicates that the neighbor relation is not considered for HO (e.g. because neighbor cell information is not available).

available:
Indicates that the neighbor relation is considered for HO if not blacklisted, i.e. if handoverAllowed is not set to 'forbidden'.

invalid:
Indicates that the neighbor relation is considered as not reliable because a CGI measurement reported a different CGI for the PCI of the neighbor cell the neighbor relation refers to or because eNB detected a conflict with another existing neighbor relation. [LTE2466 updated]
Invalid may also indicate that the neighbor relation is not considered as it is a CSG or Hybrid cell.
The nrStatus of a blacklisted neighbor relation may be nevertheless ‘available’. This indicates that all information for HO is available and HO would be in principle possible if blacklisting would be released.

LNREL instances with nrStatus 'unavailable' or 'invalid'
- do not contribute to the limit which is configured with ANRPRL parameters nrLimitIntraFreq or nrLimitInterFreq
- are not counted for triggering X2-link establishment

Full name: Min. non-GBR data for using unlicensed carrier
Short description:
This parameter is used for calculating the minimum amount of data “MinBufferedData” which should be buffered in the unlicensed SCell for a given Channel Access Priority Class before considering its transmission.
“MinBufferedData” for data of a given Access Priority Class “P” is derived from nongbrThreshUnlicensed as follows:

For lteUItuRegion = 'USA'
MinBufferedData = nonGbrThreshUnlicened * (Tmcot,p -1)/10,
For lteUItuRegion = 'Japan'
MinBufferedData = nonGbrThreshUnlicened * (min(4, Tmcot,p -1))/10,
where: “Tmcot,p” corresponds to the maximum continuous transmission time allowed for the respective Access Priority Class “P”, as defined in 3GPP TS 36.213.

If this parameter is set to '0', no threshold before data transmission is applied.

Note: For a definition of an 'unlicensed cell', refer to description of parameter relationships for actUnlicensedAcc.

Full name: Enable discovery signal padding for LAA
Short description:
This parameter enables or disables the padding of blank symbols of the discovery signal transmitted on an unlicensed cell in 'LAA' mode with random data. Enabling of the padding prevents other devices operating on the frequency of an unlicensed cell in 'LAA' mode from acquiring the channel during the silent symbols of the discovery signal transmission (e.g., symbol 2, 3, 9, 10). It also increases the total transmitted power per symbol and therefore reduces the possibility of transmission collision between LTE and other technologies (e.g., Wi-Fi). It is recommended to enable the discovery signal padding if an unlicensed cell in 'LAA' mode is expected to co-exist with other radio technologies (e.g., Wi-Fi).
Notes:
(1) This parameter takes effect only if the unlicensed cell is operated in 'LAA' mode, i.e., actUnlicensedAcc is set to 'LAA'.
(2) In case of modification of this parameter, all unlicensed cells related to changed LNUPR MOC will be automatically disabled and then enabled.
(3) For a definition of an 'unlicensed cell', refer to description of parameter relationships for actUnlicensedAcc.
Related features:
Defined by NIDD:
- LTE2860 Licensed-Assisted Access (https://webnei.emea.nsn-net.net/#/webnei/5a26c22d82ede1001280361f/1)

Full name: Min. non-GBR data for using unlicensed carrier
Short description:
This parameter is used for calculating the minimum amount of data “MinBufferedData” which should be buffered in the unlicensed SCell for a given Channel Access Priority Class before considering its transmission.
“MinBufferedData” for data of a given Access Priority Class “P” is derived from nongbrThreshUnlicensed as follows:

For lteUItuRegion = 'USA'
MinBufferedData = nonGbrThreshUnlicened * (Tmcot,p -1)/10,
For lteUItuRegion = 'Japan'
MinBufferedData = nonGbrThreshUnlicened * (min(4, Tmcot,p -1))/10,
where: “Tmcot,p” corresponds to the maximum continuous transmission time allowed for the respective Access Priority Class “P”, as defined in 3GPP TS 36.213.

If this parameter is set to '0', no threshold before data transmission is applied.
Related features:
Defined by NIDD:
- LTE3674 Multefire DRS transmission

Short description:
Maximum number of serving cells which can select a single (candidate) cell as an UL CoMP candidate cell. (Solution may impose additional restrictions.)  This parameter enables the operator to specify an upper limit on the parameter used. Decreasing this parameter will reduce the maximum number of SINR query requests received by a single candidate cell, and will also decrease the number of different serving cells which can simultaneously retrieve helper data from the same single helper cell.

If there is the wish to reduce the amount of processing and/or network traffic loading resulting from SINR queries, then this parameter may be reduced. By reducing this parameter the amount of (SINR) messaging overhead traveling over the system can be reduced. This might be done for example, if the GbE statistics or the on-time arrival rates for helper data indicate there is a problematic amount of network congestion.
If there is the wish to allow each helper cell to receive queries from a larger number of different serving cells, then this parameter may be increased.
This parameter impacts to candidate set selector functionality, and it is calculated in some intervals, maybe every 15mins. Thus, even it is online modifiable, it is applied with some delay.

This parameter is used to define the energy detection threshold “Xthresh” beyond which no “DRS only” transmission is allowed in an unlicensed cell.
Depending on how the lteUWiFiCoexistence parameter is configured, Xthresh is defined as follows:

If lteUWiFiCoexistence = “No WiFi”:

Xthresh = min(Tmax+10; “Xr”; ccaThreshold)

Else, if lteUWiFiCoexistence = “WiFi”:

Xthresh = min{ccaThreshold; max[-72 + 10 * log (dlChBw/20); min(Tmax; Tmax - Ta + (Ph + 10 * log(dlChBw) / 20) - pMax))]}

Where:

Ta = 5 dB
Ph = 23 dBm
pMax is the maximum output power in dBm for the carrier
Tmax = 10 * log(3.16228 * 10 -8 * dlChBw)
dlChBw is the single carrier bandwidth in MHz
“Xr” is the maximum energy detection threshold defined by the local regulatory body if set to a value different from “0” otherwise Xr = Tmax + 10. This parameter corresponds to 3GPP TS 36.213 Xr.

Each serving cell can request SINR measurements from a group of candidate cells. This parameter limits the maximum number of such candidates, which can be queried by a single serving cell.  The list of candidates is provided to each cell by a candidate selector function, which uses this parameter. If the operator wishes to reduce the amount of processing and/or network traffic loading resulting from SINR queries, then this parameter may be reduced. If the operator wishes to allow each serving cell to query a larger number of candidate cells for SINR measurements, then this parameter may be increased.

Full name: Enable discovery signal padding for LAA
Short description:
This parameter enables or disables the padding of blank symbols of the discovery signal transmitted on an unlicensed cell in 'LAA' mode with random data. Enabling of the padding prevents other devices operating on the frequency of an unlicensed cell in 'LAA' mode from acquiring the channel during the silent symbols of the discovery signal transmission (e.g., symbol 2, 3, 9, 10). It also increases the total transmitted power per symbol and therefore reduces the possibility of transmission collision between LTE and other technologies (e.g., Wi-Fi). It is recommended to enable the discovery signal padding if an unlicensed cell in 'LAA' mode is expected to co-exist with other radio technologies (e.g., Wi-Fi).
Note : This parameter takes effect only if the unlicensed cell is operated in 'LAA' mode, i.e., actUnlicensedAcc is set to 'LAA'.

Specifies the share of the cell resource group on a percentage basis.

Because TDD has less DL and UL TTIs per frame, so in order to have enough chances to be scheduled, TDD's value range shall be within 25 % and 75 %.
Lower bound 25% is decided based on uplink scheduling. There are 4 UL TTIs per frame, it is expected that each CRG will be scheduled at least once per frame for both downlink and uplink, so CRG share is set to start from 25%.

Then upper bound is 100%-25%=75%.

Short description:
Activate advanced step-wise SCell addition.
If this parameter is set to 'oneStepAdvanced', and step-wise cell addition is enabled (numTxWithHighNonGbr is not equal to '0'), one step SCell addition occurs when the UE enters the cell.
If this parameter is set to 'buffer-based', and step-wise cell addition is enabled, the eNB starts buffer measurements when the UE enters the cell.  Upon buffer overflows, one step SCell addition occurs if no SCells are configured for this UE, otherwise step-wise addition is performed.
If this parameter is 'off', and step-wise cell addition is enabled, the eNB starts buffer measurements when the UE enters the cell, and step-wise cell addition is performed upon buffer overflows.

The parameter determines the expiration time of an SINR average.  At a high level, if the SINR has not been updated for longer than this parameter value (e.g. because the UE has not transmitted on the uplink for some seconds), then that SINR average cannot be used to make a decision to request helper data.  As the value increases, then ULCoMP can be performed more often, i.e. on the very first uplink transmission after a longer interval of inactivity.

Short description:
The parameter determines the expiration time of an SINR average.  At a high level, if the SINR has not been updated for longer than this parameter's value (e.g. because the UE has not transmitted on the uplink for some seconds), then that SINR average cannot be used to make a decision to request helper data.  As the value increases, then ULCoMP can be performed more often, i.e. on the very first uplink transmission after a longer interval of inactivity.

Setting this to a longer value enables ULCoMP benefits for UEs with infrequent packets to gain additional ULCoMP benefit.  However, setting this to longer value also increases the risk that UEs will combine "unhelpful helper data" based upon out of the SINR information.

The SM configured value will overwrite any locally HUB configured value.

The HUB will learn the configured value from the SM.

Full name: SCell frequency layer priority for carrier aggregation
Short description:
sFreqPrio enters into the comparison between two candidate SCells. This comparison is based on a measure of the average load in uplink, and can be biased towards a cell by giving it a higher priority.
It is also used in the relative comparison to pFreqPrio in the PCell swap algorithm.
Use sFreqPrio = 1 (default) for highest priority, sFreqPrio = 10000 for lowest priority.

Note: To prioritize unlicensed against licensed cells, their sFreqPrio values shall be at least one decade apart (for example, CADPRLAA-sFreqPrio configured to be within [1-10], and CADPR-sFreqPrio or CAPR-sFreqPrio within [100-10000]).

Short description:
This parameter controls the enabling/disabling of the A3 measurements for SCell discovery and corresponding A3 event reporting.
The setting of this flag conditions the way how the SCells to add are selected as follows:
-	If the A3 measurement has been enabled on a frequency that the UE can measure without measurement gaps, SCells on such frequency will be added only if detected by the UE with sufficient quality (i.e. with power and quality level above the defined scellMeasThreshRsrq and scellMeasThreshRsrp parameter values).
-	If the A3 measurement for SCell discovery has been not enabled on a frequency, SCells on such frequency are added blindly.
-	If the A3 measurement for SCell discovery has been enabled on a frequency that the UE cannot measure without measurement gaps, SCells on such frequency are added blindly only if there is no choice from the previous two cases.

The events A3 for SCell discovery measurement are configured with “reportOnLeave” and “reportAmount=1”.

When this feature is activated the following IP addresses should be set to 0.0.0.0: IPNO-cPlaneIpAddress, IPNO-mPlaneIpAddress, IPNO-sPlaneIpAddress, IPNO-uPlaneIpAddress, IEIF-localIpAddr, IEIF-NetMask, IPRT-staticRoutes::gateway, IPSECC-securityPolicies::localTunnelEndpoint. Moreover, if operator creates VLAN (IVIF) object, then the operator should set the vlanId to 0 and the following IP addresses to 0.0.0.0: IEIF/IVIF-localIpAddr, IEIF/IVIF-netmask (the eNB shall send CCN to iOMS/NetAct to update the values for the above attributes).

Full name: M3 wait Time before starting SCTP init
Short description:
This parameter defines the M3 wait time the eNB waits until it tries to re-initialize the SCTP association
Case A: after having tried unsuccessfully to establish an association to a peer with an SCTP sequence
Case B: After reception of SCTP SHUTDOWN/ABORT
The value defines a fixed time period. In addition, eNB adds an equally distributed random time period between 0 and 10s to the configured value.

This prevents the eNBs to which the network element that has sent the SCTP shutdown command (e.g. MME) will be overflooded by SCTP initialization from multiple eNBs.
Related features:
Defined by NIDD:
- LTE3555 Separate value of SCTP wait timer for S1, X2 and M3 (https://webnei.emea.nsn-net.net/#/webnei/59f32950cf0d84001c85bee2/1)

Full name: Extended averaging window length for actual EIRP control
Short description:
If eirpLongCtrlWin is set to 'false',
- the control of actual EIRP in LTE works with internal control periods of 120 ms to realize the configured eirpReduction value. Depending on traffic scenarios, traffic bursts are served up to cell capacity and the configured eirpReduction is maintained within a maximum of 4..7 such periods.
- eirpAvgWinLen controls PM counters only.
- Established GBR bearers have their average PRB usage reserved over this time.
- The configured EIRP budget is maintained already within 1 s.

If actEirpLongCtrlWin is set to 'true',
- the duration of the control periods is increased, depending on the configured value of eirpAvgWinLen, i.e. PM counter reporting and controlling the averaged (actual) EIRP are done on the same timing basis.
- PRB reservation for GBR is no longer based on measured short-term averages. Reserving PRBs for GBR must be done by setting eirpMinNumPrbsForLte to a desired value.
Related features:
Defined by NIDD:
- LTE5574 Enhancement of actual EIRP control for non-beamforming cells (https://feature-corner.nsn-net.net/materials/cl8u9708t1194624xkzf7vyr79y)

Short description:
This parameter specifies the reduction value on the actual EIRP (Effective Isotropic Radiated Power) which reduces actual EIRP generation to a level below the 'zero' point.
The starting value ('zero' point) for the EIRP reduction for a cell is calculated from configuration data (pMax, antGainNonBF, power reduction factors) and is assumed to have contributions from all configured antennas and RF amplifiers (supercell, MIMO, TxDiv). PRB blanking (LTE3145 Slim carrier, LTE1800 DL interference shaping) affects the selection of particular PRBs by the DL scheduler but has no effect on EIRP control.

Note that using high values for EIRP reduction translates into severe capacity reductions (down to 1/4 = 25% if set at 6 dB). In particular 3 MHz or 5 MHz cells can end up being incapable of handling any reasonable traffic volumes.

Full name: Set GBR traffic to priority over a reduction of actual EIRP
Short description:
Control of actual EIRP divides traffic into two types:
- prioritized traffic is allowed to generate any level of actual EIRP. Prioritized traffic always includes MBMS, CatM, NB-IoT, HARQ retransmissions, Control Channels, and reference symbols.
- If eirpReduction is configured to a value greater than 0, non-prioritized traffic receives fewer resources, in order to maintain the EIRP reduction over the whole traffic. Non-prioritized traffic always includes non-GBR.

If eirpSetGbrOverEirp is set to 'false',
- GBR and 'duty' parts of Nominal Bit Rate (NBR) traffic are treated as non-prioritized.
- GBR still has scheduling priority over non-GBR traffic.
- the cell can compensate bursts of excessive prioritized traffic by restricting GBR and non-GBR allocations.

If eirpSetGbrOverEirp is set to 'true',
- GBR is also treated as prioritized traffic.
- only DL non-GBR traffic can be restricted in order to control actual EIRP.
- GBR traffic can generate any level of EIRP, without consideration of the configured eirpReduction.
- This can violate local regulation.

Short description:
This parameter defines mode of peer's IKE identity verification.

If the parameter is not configured or is set to ‘ACCEPT_ANY’, then BTS compares peer’s IKE identity received during IKE_AUTH exchange with identities defined in the peer’s certificate. BTS accepts establishment of the IKE SA only if the received peer's IKE identity matches the subject or subjectAltNames contained in the valid peer's certificate.

If the parameter is set to ‘PROPOSE_AND_VERIFY’ or ‘VERIFY’, BTS uses expected peer's IKE identity, configured in the parameter peerIkeIdentity of the corresponding IPsec policy, for verification of the peer's identity received during IKE_AUTH exchange.

If the parameter is set to “PROPOSE_AND_VERIFY”, then:
- BTS as initiator sends IDr payload with the expected peer's IKE identity in the IKE_AUTH request.
- BTS as initiator or responder compares peer's IKE identity received during IKE_AUTH exchange with the expected peer's IKE identity. It accepts establishment of the IKE SA only if the compared identities match.

If the parameter is set to “VERIFY”, then BTS compares the expected peer's IKE identity with identities defined in the peer's certificate received during IKE_AUTH exchange. It accepts establishment of the IKE SA only if the expected peer's IKE identity matches the subject or subjectAltNames contained in the valid peer's certificate. In this mode, BTS supports configuration of wildcards in the expected peer's IKE identity.

Default value: ‘ACCEPT_ANY’.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
Related features:
Defined by NIDD:
- LTE3978 FZM Dynamic IP for multiple tunnels (https://webnei.emea.nsn-net.net/#/webnei/59e5ac7de4b8630012e3922d/1)

Full name: MCS shift when UE enters into DL Unicast MBSFN
Short description:

- This is used when switching into DL Unicast MBSFN (e.g. to preemptively offset for link adaptation):
- Upon 1st Tx on DL Unicast MBSFN, apply this configurable MCS shift
- E.g. if upon "arriving" to the DL Unicast MBSFN for the 1st time the MCS would normally be 1 and this parameter is 4, then a MCS of 0 is used.
- E.g. if upon "arriving" to the DL Unicast MBSFN for the 1st time the MCS would normally be 8 and this parameter is 4, then a MCS of 4 is used.

Full name: Max DL unicast MBSFN subframe pattern share
Short description:
Defines the maximum Unicast MBSFN subframe pattern share based on the proportion of the system capacity that shall be reserved for Unicast PDSCH over MBSFN.
The uMbsfnShareMax should be at least 30%, i.e. this is a "strong" recommendation.
E.g. a value of 50 represents the operator desire that at most 50% of subframes are reserved for Unicast PDSCH over MBSFN and 50% is left for normal subframe (nsf) PDSCH.
This parameter impacts the calculation of the value of subframeAllocation(fourFrames) defined in TS36.331 and sent in SIB2, i.e. corresponding to uMbsfnShareUsed.
The eNB automatically selects a MBSFN subframe configuration pattern which is both:
- consistent with other enabled features (ETWS/CMAS, OTDOA), and other factors e.g. related to CSI-RS,  and
- will be less than or equal to uMbsfnShareMax
Related features:
Defined by NIDD:
- LTE4613 TM9 in MBSFN subframes (https://webnei.emea.nsn-net.net/#/webnei/5bb6f93c092dda00183dd08f/1)

A value of 50 indicates 50% of subframes are reserved for Unicast MBSFN and 50% is left for non-MBSFN (i.e. nsf or normal subframes).

Short description: The parameter is used to determine when to trigger the PIM Performance Measurement Threshold 2 Exceeded fault. The fault is issued if the antenna PIM performance measurement exceeds the PIM Cancellation Minor Threshold value for a fixed raise fault delay. Short description:

Full name: Local Traffic Selector Port number for the local IP address
Short description:
This is the port number of the local IP address. If value -1 is configured, the IPSec policy is valid in the same way to and from all ports of the local IP address.

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, local and remote port numbers  and protocol are feasible:
- single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.

The combination of localIpAddress/localIpPort/localIpPrefixLength/protocol need to be always specified for a traffic selector.
The default value is -1 and all ports are allowed.
Note: This parameter is valid for macro BTS only.

Full name: Four layer MIMO average spectral efficiency
Short description:
The four layer MIMO average spectral efficiency is used by the throughput check during step-wise SCell addition (numTxWithHighNonGBR>0) as follows.
If the throughput metric after the SCell addition is greater than the throughput metric before the SCell addition then this SCell addition is admitted. Otherwise this SCell addition is rejected. The throughput metric is the sum of xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff*bandwidth of the UE’s serving cells. Where xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff is equal to twoLayerMimoAvSpectralEff if the UE is configured with two layer MIMO on a given serving cell respectively xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff is equal to fourLayerMimoAvSpectralEff if the UE is configured with four layer MIMO on a given serving cell.

A reasonable value of the parameter can be derived from the existing KPI LTE_5747a "DL Spectral efficiency" as follows. The KPI shall be collected in conditions where all UEs are four layer MIMO capable in this cell in order not to underestimate the average value (with dlMimoMode set to "Closed Loop MIMO (4x4)").

The throughput check is not used by setting the parameter value to "0.5" i.e. any SCell addition will be always admitted by the check if twoLayerMimoAvSpectralEff = fourLayerMimoAvSpectralEff in all involved cells.

Full name: Two layer MIMO average spectral efficiency
Short description:
The two layer MIMO average spectral efficiency is used by the throughput check during step-wise SCell addition (numTxWithHighNonGBR>0) as follows.
If the throughput metric after the SCell addition is greater than the throughput metric before the SCell addition then this SCell addition is admitted. Otherwise this SCell addition is rejected. The throughput metric is the sum of xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff*bandwidth of the UE’s serving cells. Where xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff is equal to twoLayerMimoAvSpectralEff if the UE is configured with two layer MIMO on a given serving cell respectively xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff is equal to fourLayerMimoAvSpectralEff if the UE is configured with four layer MIMO on a given serving cell.

A reasonable value of the parameter can be derived from the existing KPI LTE_5747a "DL Spectral efficiency" with dlMimoMode set to "Closed Loop Mimo" or "Closed Loop MIMO (4x2)" or "Closed Loop MIMO (8x2)".

The throughput check is not used by setting the parameter value to "0.5" i.e. any SCell addition will be always admitted by the check if twoLayerMimoAvSpectralEff = fourLayerMimoAvSpectralEff in all involved cells.

Full name: Two layer MIMO average spectral efficiency
Short description:
The two layer MIMO average spectral efficiency is used by the throughput check during step-wise SCell addition (numTxWithHighNonGBR>0) as follows.
If the throughput metric after the SCell addition is greater than the throughput metric before the SCell addition then this SCell addition is admitted. Otherwise this SCell addition is rejected. The throughput metric is the sum of xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff*bandwidth of the UE’s serving cells. Where xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff is equal to twoLayerMimoAvSpectralEff if the UE is configured with two layer MIMO on a given serving cell respectively xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff is equal to fourLayerMimoAvSpectralEff if the UE is configured with four layer MIMO on a given serving cell.

A reasonable value of the parameter can be derived from the existing KPI LTE_5747a "DL Spectral efficiency" with dlMimoMode set to "Closed Loop Mimo" or "Closed Loop MIMO (4x2)".

The throughput check is not used by setting the parameter value to "0.5" i.e. any SCell addition will be always admitted by the check if twoLayerMimoAvSpectralEff = fourLayerMimoAvSpectralEff in all involved cells.

The four layer MIMO average spectral efficiency is used by the throughput check during step-wise SCell addition (numTxWithHighNonGBR>0) as follows.
If the throughput metric after the SCell addition is greater than the throughput metric before the SCell addition then this SCell addition is admitted. Otherwise this SCell addition is rejected. The throughput metric is the sum of xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff*bandwidth of the UE’s serving cells. Where xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff is equal to twoLayerMimoAvSpectralEff if the UE is configured with two layer MIMO on a given serving cell respectively xLayerMimoAvSpectralEff is equal to fourLayerMimoAvSpectralEff if the UE is configured with four layer MIMO on a given serving cell.

A reasonable value of the parameter can be derived from the existing KPI LTE_5747a "DL Spectral efficiency" as follows. The KPI shall be collected in conditions where all UEs are four layer MIMO capable in this cell in order not to underestimate the average value (with dlMimoMode set to "Closed Loop MIMO (4x4)" or "Closed Loop MIMO (8x4)").

The throughput check is not used by setting the parameter value to "0.5" i.e. any SCell addition will be always admitted by the check if twoLayerMimoAvSpectralEff = fourLayerMimoAvSpectralEff in all involved cells.
Related features:

- LTE2532 TDD downlink carrier aggregation with 4 layers MIMO (https://webnei.emea.nsn-net.net/#/webnei/591074edbbd2c64b0d6a9bcf/1)

Full name: Idle session time for Transport Web Page
Short description:

A value of 0 indicates not to monitor user activity.
